A 85-year-old male visits his primary care physician due to concerns about difficulty achieving an
erection. He reports that since having a heart attack one month ago, he has been unable to maintain
an erection despite finding his wife sexually attractive and wanting to engage in intercourse. He
mentions feeling guilty about this and experiencing a depressed mood, along with reduced energy and
less interest in his hobby of working on motorcycles. His medications were started after the heart
attack. Vital signs show a temperature of 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure of 134/94 mmHg, pulse of
95/min, respirations of 12/min, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Physical examination
reveals an obese man with normal external genitalia and 1+ dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses.
His gait, strength, and sensation are normal. What is the most likely cause of this patient’s symptoms?
Answer Choices: (A) Cardiovascular deconditioning (B) Aortoiliac occlusion (C) Depression (D)
Medication side effect (E) Performance anxiety disorder (F) Anxiety (G) Peripheral vascular disease
(H) Psychogenic erectile dysfunction (I) Testosterone deficiency (J) Post-MI autonomic dysfunction
 A. Post-MI autonomic dysfunction
B. Anxiety
C. Depression
D. Testosterone deficiency
E. Aortoiliac occlusion
F. Psychogenic erectile dysfunction
G. Peripheral vascular disease
H. Medication side effect
I. Cardiovascular deconditioning
J. Performance anxiety disorder
